sections.content: JOINs combine tables on related columns: INNER JOIN keeps only matching rows, LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows (NULLs where no match), RIGHT/FULL cover the other side.
ON specifies the match condition (usually foreign key = primary key). Joins multiply rows when matches are one-to-many.
Key points: pick the join type by which side must survive, alias tables (u.name) for readability, and check row counts — accidental cartesian products explode results.
